label: The Kauffman Bracket
notes: Open the lecture. The Kauffman bracket is a deceptively simple state sum that, once corrected for writhe, yields the Jones polynomial. The lecture defines the bracket through a skein rule on unoriented diagrams, computes it on small examples, and explains why it is only a regular isotopy invariant rather than a full knot invariant.

label: The Bracket Skein Rule
notes: State the defining rule: at each crossing the bracket splits into two smoothings, an A-smoothing and a B-smoothing, weighted by the variable A and its inverse. This local relation, applied at every crossing, expands any diagram into a sum over all states, each a disjoint union of simple loops. The rule is purely combinatorial.

label: Loops and Normalization
notes: Fix the value of a single loop to one and decree that an extra disjoint loop multiplies the bracket by minus A squared minus A to the minus two. Together with the skein rule these conventions determine the bracket of any diagram as a Laurent polynomial in A obtained by summing over every state of the diagram.

label: Regular Isotopy
notes: Show that the bracket is invariant under the second and third Reidemeister moves but changes by a factor under the first. Hence it is a regular isotopy invariant rather than a true knot invariant. The first move introduces a curl whose writhe must be tracked and later cancelled to repair the defect.

label: Worked Example
notes: Compute the bracket of the trefoil by resolving its three crossings into eight states and collecting powers of A. The resulting Laurent polynomial is nontrivial, distinguishing the trefoil diagram from the unknot. The calculation illustrates how the state sum grows but remains entirely mechanical and finite for any diagram.

label: Recap
notes: Close the lecture. The Kauffman bracket is a state sum defined by a smoothing skein rule and a loop value, invariant under the second and third Reidemeister moves but not the first. Correcting for writhe in the next lecture turns this regular isotopy invariant into the celebrated Jones polynomial.
